_comment: Taxonomy for areas/aml-transcriptomics, 186 papers. Drawn by reading each paper's abstract, discussion and key points; every paper in exactly one topic. Six parts follow the layers at which AML is dysregulated, from the initiating lesion outward.

parts.name: RNA processing: splicing, isoforms and modification
Stem cells, heterogeneity and disease evolution

topics.name: RUNX1::RUNX1T1 and the t(8;21) regulatory network
topics.description: How the most common AML fusion rewires transcription: what it binds, which cofactors it brings, and how it activates as well as represses. The subtype with the most complete mechanistic account in this collection, and the one where that account is still being revised.

topics.name: t(8;21): dependencies, cooperating lesions and stem cells
topics.description: What t(8;21) leukemia needs in order to persist. Cure rates exceed 60% and roughly half of patients still relapse, so the papers here are about the preleukemic reservoir and the cooperating events rather than about initial response.

topics.name: KMT2A rearrangement and the menin-MLL axis
topics.description: The subtype that produced the field's most advanced targeted therapy and its most instructive failure. Menin inhibition works, responses are incomplete, resistance is fast - and several papers here are about why.

topics.name: NPM1 mutation: mislocalisation, chromatin and HOX
topics.description: The most common lesion in adult AML, defined by a protein leaving the nucleus - and recently shown to act on chromatin anyway. Two independent groups overturned the standing loss-of-function model in the same journal issue.

topics.name: NUP98, DEK::NUP214, EVI1 and other rearrangements
topics.description: Rare fusions, each with its own dependency. Individually these entities are too small to study in a trial, which is why a shared mechanism - XPO1, HOXA activation, enhancer hijacking - matters more here than elsewhere.

topics.name: Chromatin regulators and readers as therapeutic dependencies
topics.description: Wild-type chromatin proteins co-opted to hold the differentiation block, which the field increasingly prefers as targets over the transcription factors they serve. Several of these papers correct what a drug in trials was thought to be doing.

topics.name: DNA methylation, TET/IDH and the mutational landscape
topics.description: Methylation as cause rather than consequence, and the metabolic lesions that write it. Includes the ageing hematopoietic stem cell, which arrives at an AML-like epigenome before any driver mutation does.

topics.name: Chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organisation
topics.description: Where the genome is open and what is looped to what. The measurements are recent enough that the largest single-cancer epigenomic dataset ever assembled is in this topic, and it finds subtypes no genetic classification contains.

topics.name: Splicing factor mutations and splicing-directed therapy
topics.part_name: RNA processing: splicing, isoforms and modification
topics.description: Mutations in SRSF2, U2AF1 and SF3B1 are always heterozygous and never co-occur, which predicts a synthetic lethality and has driven a whole therapeutic programme. The prediction holds; the therapeutic window is narrower than hoped.

topics.name: Splicing regulators and RNA-binding proteins as dependencies
topics.part_name: RNA processing: splicing, isoforms and modification
topics.description: The proteins that decide which isoform gets made, and what happens when a leukemia needs one of them more than a normal cell does. This is where most of the collection's genuinely AML-selective targets are.

topics.name: m6A and the epitranscriptome
topics.part_name: RNA processing: splicing, isoforms and modification
topics.description: Writers, erasers and readers of the most abundant internal mRNA modification, all of which turn out to matter in AML. The direction is not conserved across tissues, which is a caution as much as a finding.

topics.name: Long-read transcriptomics, circular and chimeric RNAs
topics.part_name: RNA processing: splicing, isoforms and modification
topics.description: What short reads cannot see. Every increase in sequencing depth reveals more transcripts, which is either evidence of untapped complexity or of an error rate - and the papers here disagree about which.

topics.name: Oxidative metabolism and chemoresistance
topics.description: The finding that reorganised the field: cells surviving chemotherapy are not quiescent stem cells but metabolically distinct ones. Almost everything else in this part descends from it.

topics.name: BCL2 family dependencies and venetoclax response
topics.description: Venetoclax changed AML treatment and is not curative. These papers are about who responds, why the others do not, and whether the standard explanation - monocytic differentiation - survives contact with patient data.

topics.name: Lipid, amino acid and cofactor metabolism as vulnerabilities
topics.description: Metabolic dependencies beyond the respiratory chain, several of them created by the leukemia's own adaptations. The recurring problem is that the pathway is usually essential in normal cells too.

topics.name: TP53 alteration and complex karyotype
topics.description: The group every other strategy in this collection excludes. Median survival is six to nine months, p53-restoring approaches have failed in trials, and the papers here are mostly about working around p53 rather than through it.

topics.name: Leukaemic stem cells, dormancy and relapse
topics.part_name: Stem cells, heterogeneity and disease evolution
topics.description: The cancer stem cell model of relapse, and the primary work that contests it. Whether the relapse-initiating cell is a stem cell or a transient state that any cell can enter is not settled inside this topic.

topics.name: Single-cell atlases of AML heterogeneity
topics.part_name: Stem cells, heterogeneity and disease evolution
topics.description: Resources rather than results, and the reason several other topics here could be written. Expression alone cannot tell a malignant cell from a normal one in a disease that recapitulates hematopoiesis, so genotype has to be read from the same cell.

topics.name: Transcriptome-based diagnosis, classification and risk
topics.description: The argument that one RNA-seq assay should replace the current patchwork of cytogenetics, FISH and targeted panels - with the validation work that claim requires, and the populations for whom the existing panels were never built.

topics.name: Immunotherapy, immune evasion and the microenvironment
topics.description: AML has one approved therapeutic antibody and a low mutational burden. These papers look for antigens, for the reasons T cells fail here, and for ways to make a cold tumour visible.

topics.name: Functional genomics screens as target-discovery platforms
topics.description: Screens read as method rather than as result: what changes when you screen in vivo instead of in culture, in primary cells instead of lines, or filter hits against human genetics before believing them.
